plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in cool autumn temperatures and is a staple of fall gardens and floral displays.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide in the Northern Hemisphere; native to East Asia
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the November birth flower and are honored in Japan with an annual festival and as the emblem of the Imperial family.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that erupts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Its blooms carpet streets and gardens as spring advances in the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Australia, South Africa, Argentina, and Brazil; native to South America
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas bloom each year, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that flowers in autumn, earlier than most camellias. It produces delicate, often fragrant single or semi-double blossoms against glossy dark green foliage, providing nectar to pollinators late in the season.
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and mild temperate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall native North American wildflower with showy daisy-like flower heads that have purple rays around yellow centers. It brightens meadows and roadsides in late fall and is an important food source for migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in meadows, prairies, and roadsides
plants.funFact: New England Aster flower heads close up at night and on cloudy days, then reopen with the sun.
